title: A streamed response body cannot be cut off by the program, so an unfinished download ends as if it were complete.
text: `rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream` says a `Workbook::createForDownload` that is never finished is cut off, so the browser reports a failed download and not a broken file. Nothing can ask for that today. `nvs_runtime::stream::Emit` has one ending, `finish`, and its `Drop` calls it (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/stream.rs:260` and `:279`), so an isolate that ends for any reason ends its body cleanly: `Drain::next_chunk` answers `Drained::Ended`, and the streaming body here answers `Poll::Ready(None)`, the end of a complete body. The body already has the other ending for the drain period: it answers an error frame (`DrainPeriodEnded`) when the cut is reached, which aborts the response. Closing the gap means a second ending on `Emit`, an abort that `Drain` reports and this body turns into that same error frame, and a way for the Novis half to ask for it when the request ends with a workbook still open. Today only the guest notices that, as the error it logs when its `writer` is dropped unfinished. Until then the unfinished workbook is logged and the browser saves a truncated archive.
